title: Feature Track Bookkeeping with set, unordered_set & set algorithms
hints: `std::set<int> a(prev.begin(), prev.end());` sorts and dedups in one line. Its iteration is ascending.
`std::set_intersection(a.begin(), a.end(), b.begin(), b.end(), std::back_inserter(out))` needs **sorted** ranges, which a std::set gives you. `set_difference(a, b)` gives a \ b.
countUniqueVoxels: `std::set<std::tuple<int,int,int>>` works out of the box because tuple has `operator<`. Remember `std::floor` for negative coordinates.
hasDuplicateIds: `unordered_set::insert` returns `{iterator, bool inserted}`. The first `false` is a duplicate, so you can stop early.
